## Conclusion
- **Pick: Xiaomi TV S Pro Mini LED 75 2026, wall-mounted** (S$2,199, was S$2,599; Xiaomi Official Store, 3-year on-site warranty) — 75" 4K 144Hz, 704-zone QD-Mini LED, 1700 nits peak, at roughly half the price of tier-one equivalents; the weak built-in speakers don't matter because KEF handles audio.
- **It fits his use**: PS5 Pro 4K120 + VRR, KEF over eARC and Switch 2 at 4K60 can all be connected at once; the only loss is Switch 2's 120Hz mode.
- **HDMI plan**: HDMI 1 → PS5 Pro; HDMI 2 (eARC) → KEF LS50 Wireless II; HDMI 3 → Switch 2.
- **Bracket: Vogel's TVM 5605** (15 mm from the wall, VESA up to 600×400, 100 kg, about £93) — the Singapore box has no wall bracket; Xiaomi's install service (75" fixed, S$161 incl. bracket) **excludes wallpaper walls and third-party brackets**, and this TV wall has joinery + wallpaper, so Patrick installs it.

- **4K120 ports**: PS5 Pro needs 4K120 + VRR; only HDMI 1/2 run 144Hz, and HDMI 2 is also the eARC port.

- **Wall depth**: thinner looks better; plugs must hide in a recessed box.

## In one line
- **BPI2638UB** = power model: two 3.6 kW zones (incl. a 28 cm large zone), **needs a dedicated 32A circuit**, 7.4 kW total. S$1,459–1,480.
- **BPI6603B** = flexible-circuit model: **power cap settable 13–32A** (1.5–7.1 kW), so it can run off a 13A socket; heat scales down with the cap. S$1,100.

## Watch out
- **BPI2638UB**: a dedicated 32A circuit from the DB + double-pole isolator, hard-wired (no plug); cut-out 56 × 49.
- **BPI6603B**: at a low cap, several zones together auto-throttle; per-zone power isn't published; cut-out 56.5 × 49.5.
- **Both**: 60 cm, anti-scratch glass, body about 5.4 below the worktop → vent gap above the drawer below; pick an oven with a cooling fan.

## Recommendation
- **Get the BPI2638UB**: the new kitchen gets a fresh 32A circuit anyway, so the 6603B's flexible-circuit advantage is wasted; the 2638UB has more power and clear specs — worth the extra S$380.
- Only switch to the BPI6603B (set to 20A or 13A) if a 32A circuit can't be run (DB capacity).

## Criteria
- **Zone power**: a large zone of ≥ 3.5 kW for stockpots and woks, and a strong second zone.
- **Total power × circuit**: on a dedicated 32A circuit the hob should be able to use all of it.
- **Glass**: anti-scratch (Crystal Protect / anti-scratch) black glass against the sintered-stone worktop.
- **Size**: 60 cm slot, cut-out ≤ 56.5 × 49.5, body depth must clear the drawer below.
- **Controls**: touch; a slider is quicker, +/− keys are fine.
- **Local warranty and installation**: 2-year Brandt warranty in Singapore, hard-wired to 32A.

## Decision
- **Pick: Apple Home as the only app + Aqara Hub M3 (Zigbee backbone) + the HomePod mini already owned as the home hub (S$0)** — switches, sensors and light strips run Zigbee to M3, bridged into Apple Home via HomeKit; the HomePod mini handles remote access, automations, HKSV analysis, Thread border routing and Matter control.
- **The Frame cannot replace the hub**: the Apple TV on the TV is only a streaming app (plus AirPlay 2); Samsung TVs never appear in Apple Home's home-hub list and are not Apple Thread border routers. Only a HomePod, HomePod mini or Apple TV box can be the hub. The Frame has its own SmartThings hub (with Matter/Thread), but that is a second app and is not needed.
- **Alternative: Apple TV 4K (4th generation, A19, Wi-Fi + Ethernet, S$399, in stores 13 Nov)** — buy only if HKSV events from the three E1s are often missed or late, or the HomePod mini often shows 'No Response'; it then becomes the active hub automatically and the HomePod mini goes to standby.
- **No second HomePod mini**: Apple uses only one active hub at a time; M3 is already a second Thread border router. Buy one later only for bedroom audio.
- **Alternative architecture: everything Matter over Thread, direct** — 86-box Thread switches and UK-plug Thread plugs have almost no local stock in Singapore; revisit in 2–3 years.
- **Rejected: Aqara Home as the main app; extra Hue / SwitchBot / Tuya hubs** — another account and another failure point.
- **Network: UniFi U7 Lite ×2 + Cloud Gateway Ultra (S$219) + USW Lite 8 PoE** — the gateway replaces the ISP router and runs UniFi Network; without it APs run in standalone mode, configured one by one, with no fast roaming or remote management. Buy: UI Store SG online, or authorised reseller Win-Pro (38 Jalan Pemimpin #07-04 M38); no shop with display units found.
- **Main-door scene button: Aqara Wireless Remote Switch H1 (Double Rocker), S$45** — single/double/long press per rocker + both together, up to 7 Apple Home scenes; battery about 5 years, no wiring.
- **No UPS**: Singapore's 2024 SAIDI was 0.26 minutes per customer, under 1 minute of outage a year on average.
- **iCloud+ 200 GB**: required for HKSV on 3 E1 cameras (50 GB allows 1, 200 GB up to 5); recordings do not count against storage.
- **By category**: switches Aqara Smart Wall Switch H1 EU (with neutral); cameras Aqara Camera E1 + HKSV; plugs Tapo P110M; lights plain downlights + Aqara LED Strip T1; sensors Aqara door sensor + Motion Sensor P1.

## Criteria
- **Works offline**: wall switches cut power directly; the scene button runs on the HomePod mini locally, no internet needed.
- **One app, easy family sharing**: daily use is Apple Home only; family are invited with Apple accounts, no Aqara account.
- **Singapore stock and warranty**: BS 86 mm boxes, BS1363 plugs, 12–36-month local warranty; imports only when there is no alternative.
- **≤ 2 hubs, reuse what is owned**: HomePod mini + M3; no other device may need its own hub.
- **Native Apple Home features**: Adaptive Lighting requires HomeKit bridging (lost via Matter bridging); cameras need HKSV.
- **Power-loss recovery**: switches set to power-off memory so lights stay off; no UPS (outages are very rare in Singapore).
- **Long-term support**: models on the market ≥ 2 years and still updated (H1, E1, M3).

## Next steps
- **Tell the electrician (switches)**: neutral N to every switch box; 86 mm square boxes ≥ 35 mm deep; max 2 circuits per H1 plate.
- **Tell the electrician (strips and network)**: always-live power at each strip driver; one Cat6 at the TV cabinet for M3 (PoE) + one spare for a future Apple TV.
- **HomePod mini placement**: central living room, near an AP, not inside a closed cabinet; it becomes the hub automatically once set up.
- **Setup**: add M3 to Apple Home with the HomeKit QR and do not add it again via Matter; set M3's Thread to join Apple's network; Zigbee channel 25, 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi fixed on 1 or 6; keep HomePod mini, cameras and plugs on one subnet.
- **Main-door scene button**: Wireless Remote Switch H1 double rocker; left single press 'Leave' (all lights and plugs off), right single press 'Arrive', the rest custom.

## Risks and open items
> ⚠️ HomePod mini is Wi-Fi only: if Wi-Fi drops, remote access and Apple Home automations stop; wall switches and M3 local automations keep working.
> ⚠️ HKSV analysis runs on the hub; Apple does not publish how many cameras a HomePod mini can handle (TBC). If the three E1s often miss events, that is the signal to buy an Apple TV.
> ⚠️ HomePod mini and M3 are both Thread border routers; M3 must join Apple's network or the mesh splits in two.
> ⚠️ Hub M3 is a single point of failure: switches still work by hand, but app control and automations for Aqara devices (including the scene button) stop.
- HKSV records events only, not 24/7; continuous recording relies on the E1's microSD. Camera E1 is 2.4 GHz only.
- Apple Home does not yet support Matter cameras (2026-10, TBC).
- Kid's-room camera: stop streaming and recording when someone is home.

The problem is that Xiaomi states brightness and colour temperature are set only in the Mijia App. If you choose it, set 2700K and the brightness once in the App at installation; after that the remote only switches the light on and off.
- **Head to head**: both are slim, neither has a heater, and the prices are similar. SMARTLUX LITE wins on a confirmed length, local installation and warranty, and light control without the App. Mijia wins on a brighter, warmer light and telescopic rods.

## Conclusion
- **Pick: Noctua NF-A12x25 5V PWM (120×120×25 mm) + bundled USB power cable + a USB-A inline on/off switch**, powered from its own wall USB socket or USB charger, not the PS5. 56.6 CFM, 21.4 dB(A), 0.3 A, 2.07 mmH₂O static pressure — best behind wooden slats.
- **Speed control (optional)**: add a Noctua NA-FC1 knob in series (Noctua confirms it works between the USB cable and a 5V PWM fan).
- **Simplest fallback: AC Infinity MULTIFAN S3** (120×25, 52 CFM, 18 dBA, built-in OFF + 3-speed inline switch), S$51 on desertcart.sg; ~1 mmH₂O static pressure loses more airflow behind slats.
- **Skip 15 mm slim fans**: NF-A12x15 PWM saves 10 mm but is louder at full speed (23.9 dB(A)), lower pressure, and 12 V (needs a USB 5V→12V step-up cable).
- **Skip 140 mm (NF-A14 5V PWM)**: most airflow (82.5 CFM) but the 140 mm frame has no margin in a ~14 cm fan zone.
- **Skip MULTIFAN S7**: dual 120 mm, 24 cm wide — does not fit.

## Is the airflow enough
- CFM ≈ 1.76 × W ÷ ΔT(°C). PS5 Pro ≈ 230 W → ~40 CFM for ≤10 °C rise, ~27 CFM for ≤15 °C.
- Rated CFM is free-air; behind slats expect ~60–70 % (TBC). Door is open while gaming, so intake is not the bottleneck.

## Next steps
- Measure the fan zone: ≥125×125 mm clear and 27 mm deep for a 120 mm fan with pads.

## Decision
- **Pick: KEF LS50 Wireless II ×2 on KEF S2 Floor Stands, outside both ends of console A (220, default).**
  - 252.6 between centres, about 2.45 m to the seated ears, about 54.5° included angle, close to the 60° ideal.
  - Price: KEF HK HK$18,380/pair + S2 HK$3,580/pair; Singapore price TBC.
- **Subwoofer pick: KEF KC62, beside the right stand.**
  - Reaches 11 Hz and fills in below the LS50 WII's 45 Hz; essential for movies.
  - Price: HK$13,800; Singapore price TBC.
- **Rejected: speakers on the console.** The tweeters would sit too low, below the ears, and the hollow drawer carcass resonates.
- Performance and reliability: see 'TV audio options'.

## Placement
- **Axis:** TV, console and sofa on one axis, 160 from the glass.
- **Stands:** left stand centre about 33.7 from the glass, right about 286.3, each 126.3 from the axis.
- **Direction:** face straight ahead or toe in slightly. The Uni-Q stays smooth off axis; raise Treble Trim if it sounds dull.
- **Rear wall:**
  - Speaker backs 8 from the wall, leaving room for the rear plugs to turn down into the S2 column. The LS50 WII is rear-ported.
  - KC62 back 6 from the wall. It is sealed and side-firing; KEF only asks for ≥ 7.7 between each driver and a wall.
- **Height:** tweeters about 81.

## Connections & settings
- **Primary speaker on the right** (KEF's default right channel).
- **TV:** HDMI eARC to the Xiaomi TV's eARC port with HDMI-CEC on and TV audio output set to PCM. Which HDMI port is eARC on the S Pro is TBC; keep the PS5 Pro off the eARC port.
- **Between the speakers:** inter-speaker cable through the Ø32 conduit, with Cable mode on in KEF Connect.
- **Network:** Cat6 to the primary speaker.
- **KC62:** RCA from the Sub Out, no KW1.
- **KEF Connect:**
  - Wall distance < 10 cm (Wall Mode); if the sound is thin, try 10–50 cm.
  - Bass Extension on Standard.
  - Selecting the KC62 applies its preset (70 Hz high-pass / 45 Hz low-pass).
- **KC62 unit:** LFE mode, rear EQ on Wall, volume at about 3 o'clock.
- **Sockets:** each speaker and the KC62 plug straight into their own twin 13A wall socket (KEF advises against extension strips).

## Risks / to confirm
- Singapore prices TBC.
- Stereo only: no Atmos, centre or surround channels (see 'TV audio options' for the trade-off).
- Xiaomi TV CEC wake/standby and lip-sync TBC.

en.## 結論\n- **KEF LS50 Wireless II + KC62 是:
## Conclusion
- **KEF LS50 Wireless II + KC62 is the right upgrade for this room. Buy the KC62 too; it is not optional for movies.** On its own the LS50 WII reaches 45 Hz (±3 dB) and 40 Hz (−6 dB). Erin's Audio Corner found limited output below 50 Hz and called it "excellent but not high output". The KC62 (11–200 Hz ±3 dB) handles everything below 70 Hz and adds headroom.
- **A thin sound usually comes from having no sub, or from the Wall EQ cutting too much bass.** The speakers themselves are not too small.
- **The room is a reasonable fit for moderate levels.** The zone is about 47 m³ (ceiling of 2.6 m TBC) and opens onto the corridor and kitchen. Sound & Vision called the KC62 best for small rooms and moderate levels, testing in a room of about 79 m³. Reference-level cinema volume is out of reach.
- **Adding the KEF XIO and Sennheiser AMBEO Plus does not change the pick.** The XIO is the only real alternative: it has a true centre, Atmos and DTS:X, and can take a KC62. But its stereo width is limited to the 121 cm bar, against 252.6 cm between the LS50 WIIs, and it has less music detail. The AMBEO Plus is out: vocals are vague in AMBEO mode, and it is a 2022 model now selling at clearance prices.
- **The honest trade-off is fidelity over immersion.** The system is stereo PCM 2.0 only, with no centre, surround or height channels and no Dolby decoding. In exchange, the music and dialogue quality is far better: What Hi-Fi rated the KEF's sound 5/5 and the Sony HT-X8500's 3/5.
- **Most stable set-up:** inter-speaker cable through the wall conduit, Ethernet to the primary (right) speaker, RCA from the primary's sub out to the KC62, and the TV's eARC port to the KEF HDMI input with the TV set to output PCM.

## 1. Performance in this room
- **Measured and specified figures:**
  - **LS50 WII:** 108 dB max SPL at 1 m; 280 W + 100 W per speaker.
  - **Erin's Audio Corner:** about 90 dB maximum at 4 m; sweet spot of 80–85 dB at 4 m or 90 dB at 2 m.
  - **At 2.5 m:** about 94 dB per speaker. This is an estimate scaled from Erin's figure by distance, not a measurement.
- **Wall EQ:** the speakers are rear-ported and 8 cm from the wall. The < 10 cm setting cuts the most bass. If the sound is thin, try the 10–50 cm setting.
- **Room modes (calculated):** 30.6 Hz, 52.8 Hz and 66 Hz.
- **Listening angle:** with 252.6 cm between speakers and ears about 2.45 m from the speaker plane (assumed), the included angle is about 54.5°. That is close to the ideal and works well for a phantom centre.
- **Movies:** the TV must output PCM 2.0; the TV downmixes Atmos and 5.1 to stereo. No dialogue enhancement mode was found (TBC).
- **KC62 integration:** selecting KC62 in KEF Connect applies a 70 Hz high-pass and a 45 Hz low-pass. Set the KC62 to LFE mode with the volume at about 3 o'clock. A KEF trainer suggests raising both points by 10–15 Hz if needed.

## 2. Comparison

| Sony HT-X8500 | 2.1 built-in subs; virtual Atmos/DTS:X | What Hi-Fi sound 3/5, muffled dialogue | eARC; £349 at UK launch; SG price TBC |
| Samsung HW-S801D | 3.1.2 with up-firing drivers and centre; Atmos, no DTS:X; wireless sub | Expert Reviews: clear centre dialogue, front-heavy | Mini HDMI eARC; S$524 sale / S$757 |
| HomePod (2nd gen) ×1 or ×2 | A pair supports Atmos and 5.1/7.1; no sub option | S&V Top Pick; limited max volume | Via Apple TV 4K eARC; S$429 each (2023) |
| HomePod mini ×2 | Stereo, no Dolby; no room-correction mic | Weakest bass and volume | Via Apple TV 4K eARC; S$139 each (2023) |
| KEF XIO | 5.1.2 (12 drivers incl. 6 Uni-Q MX); Atmos, DTS:X, MPEG-H; claimed 34 Hz (conditions unconfirmed); sub out + KW2 wireless, so the KC62 can be added | What Hi-Fi sound 5/5 and an Award: precise, with tight bass but less bass than the Sennheiser, so a sub is suggested. Son-Vidéo: clear centred dialogue; music is wide but has less micro-detail and vocal emotion than separate speakers | One HDMI 2.1 eARC port, no passthrough (the PS5 Pro stays on the TV); mic auto-calibration; £1,999 UK, SG price TBC |
| Sennheiser AMBEO Soundbar Plus | 7.1.4 (9 drivers + virtual); Atmos, DTS:X, 360 RA; optional AMBEO Sub (8-inch sealed, 27 Hz) | What Hi-Fi sound 5/5: wide soundfield and strong with music; vocals vague and echoey in AMBEO mode | 2 × HDMI 2.0 inputs (no 4K/120, no VRR) + eARC; 4-mic calibration; Harvey Norman S$1,199 sale (was S$2,299); AMBEO Sub S$1,099 (2023) |

## 3. Verdict and tuning
- **XIO vs LS50 WII:**
  - Switch to XIO + KC62 only if movie immersion and dialogue matter more than music. The 121 cm bar fits the 220 console.
  - For this household's music + movies + PS5 use, with 252.6 cm speaker spacing available, keep the LS50 WII + KC62.
  - The XIO launched in 2025, so there are no long-term reports yet on firmware or eARC stability (TBC).
- Choose the KEF with the KC62. If immersion matters more than fidelity, the Samsung S801D is the better pick instead.
- **Tuning:**
  - **Wall EQ:** start at < 10 cm and step up if the sound is thin.
  - **KC62:** start from the preset, set LFE mode and Wall EQ, then raise the crossover points 10–15 Hz if needed and blend with sub gain.
  - **Placement and room:** keep toe-in minimal, add Treble Trim if the sound is dull, lay a large rug and close the curtains.

## 4. Reliability
- **Inter-speaker link:** use the cable, which runs at 24/192 against 24/96 wireless. Forum dropouts were on the wireless link and caused by interference.
- **Network:** use Ethernet. Firmware v4.0 and v4.1 in 2026 still needed Wi-Fi driver fixes.
- **TV:** use eARC with the TV set to PCM. Owners have reported ARC silence and noise bursts, often fixed by PCM output or a certified cable.
- **Sub:** use RCA rather than the KW1, which has reported dropouts.
- **Firmware history:** fixes cover TV auto-switch and mute, sub wake-up, Spotify, Cast and Roon. **No firmware note mentions eARC, CEC or lip-sync.**
- **Residual risks:** CEC and standby behaviour with the Xiaomi TV (TBC), and no lip-sync adjustment in KEF Connect (TBC).

en.## 結論\n- **兩個陽台都裝、全高（地到天花）、橫向、5 cm 間距的 3:
## Decision
- **Both balconies: full-height (floor to ceiling), horizontal, 5 cm spacing, 316 cable invisible grilles.** Full height closes the opening, so a climbing child cannot get over the top. That matters more than whether the cables can be climbed.
- **One-line spec for the contractor:** "316 stainless 7×7 cable, 2.5 mm core, nylon or Teflon coated (state OD); horizontal at 5 cm c/c, full height; aluminium 6063 powder-coated track matching the window frames; stainless fixings into concrete; SETSCO/SGS tensile report for this cable; warranty ≥ 10 yr anti-rust on cable and ≥ 5 yr workmanship incl. free re-tensioning; installer handles the MCST submission."
- **Get three quotes:** Endo Grilles, Diamond Grille System, CSA Invisible Grille (reasons under 'Installers').
- **Legal:** the MCST cannot refuse a child-safety device but may set its appearance (colour, direction, spacing). Get the Sengkang Grand by-laws or renovation guidelines first.
- **BCA states** that owner-added invisible grilles are not safety barriers. The existing 1.0 m barrier must stay as it is.
- **Kid-room window:** install grilles on openable windows too (window type and opening width TBC).

## Spec differences
| Item | Options | Difference | Pick |
|---|---|---|---|
| Grade | 304 / 316(L) | 316 has molybdenum and resists chloride pitting; 304 suits inland sites with regular care | 316 |
| Core | 2 / 2.5 / 3 mm | Thicker is stronger and more visible; 2 mm is common | 2.5 mm |
| Construction | 1×19 / 7×7 / 7×19 | 1×19 is stiffest, 7×7 in between, 7×19 most flexible (more stretch) | 7×7 |
| Coating | Nylon / Teflon / bare | Coating resists abrasion and UV but ages; bare mono-core holds more tension | Coated, state OD |
| Track | Aluminium / stainless | Usually aluminium 6063-T6; must be fixed into concrete | Aluminium, powder-coated to match frames |
| Spacing | 5 / 7.5 / 10 cm | Singapore has no spacing rule for invisible grilles | 5 cm |

- **Breaking load (all vendor or web claims, and they vary widely):**
  - 316, 2.5 mm, nylon-coated to 3.5 mm: 388 kg minimum (UK supplier spec).
  - Blog table: 2.0 mm 150–200 kg, 2.5 mm 250–300 kg, 3.0 mm 350–400+ kg.
  - Diamond Grille claims 1,000 kg per wire.
  - Rely on a test report for the actual cable.
- **Spacing basis:**
  - BCA requires barriers to stop a 100 mm sphere. Invisible grilles are not statutory barriers, but 5 cm is far below that.
  - No rule separates 5 cm from 6 cm. 5 cm (about 2 in) is the tightest common local spacing; it costs more cable for a smaller gap.
- **Horizontal vs vertical:**
  - BCA counts horizontal members with gaps over 30 mm as climbable toeholds, so horizontal cables can in principle be climbed.
  - At full height there is nothing to climb over, so the local norm, horizontal, is fine.
  - Vertical cables avoid the toehold issue but need a floor track. Ask for both in the quote.
- **Lifespan:** no reliable figure. Treat the warranty period as the lower bound.

## Common problems
- **Sagging:** cables bed in and loosen within 30–90 days, and heat and cold shift tension → put a free re-tension in the contract.
- **Tea staining:** salt and iron particles break down the steel's protective surface layer and leave brown spots. Wipe with fresh water, avoid bleach and steel brushes, and passivate with citric acid if needed.
- **Coating ageing:** nylon and Teflon age in sunlight (years TBC); Teflon resists UV better but costs more.
- **Track:** an aluminium track with stainless screws risks galvanic corrosion. Ask what isolating washers the installer uses.
- **Installation:** one owner had grilles block the aircon condenser and had the balcony redone → confirm aircon service and window-cleaning access first.

## Installers
| Installer | Known | Warranty | Price |
|---|---|---|---|
| Endo Grilles | Recommended by owners on a forum, quotes on site; All Weather uses a 316 core | Premium Nylon 5 yr; All Weather 7+3 yr; Diamond Rod 15 yr | Blog: from $4.90 psf (fixed) |
| Diamond Grille System | Bare mono-core wire (no coating), higher tension | 15 yr anti-rust | TBC |
| CSA Invisible Grille | 316, typically 2 mm, custom spacing | TBC | $10–18 psf |

- **Market price (2025–26, all from vendors or blogs):** $8–10, $10–18 and $12–18 psf have all been quoted; a standard balcony is about $900–1,800. Go by actual quotes.
- **Warranty norms:** anywhere from 3–5 yr to 10–15 yr.
- **Others:** Elelaurels (5 yr, claims SETSCO), Invisible Grille Concept, Meridian, Secret Furnishing (claims 10 yr, from $8.80 psf).
- **What the quote must state:**
  - Grade, core and outer diameter, strand construction
  - Spacing (c/c) and direction
  - Track material, colour and fixing method
  - Tension or breaking load per cable, with a test report
  - Separate anti-rust and workmanship warranty periods, and how many re-tensions are included
  - How area is measured (psf or per foot) and whether the MCST submission is included
  - Cost to remove and refit the aircon and drying rack

## Look & layout
- **Visibility:**
  - From inside, the cables mostly show against the light or up close; thicker or glossier coating shows more.
  - Colours are black, silver and white. Black reads as less visible from outside; silver blends with the frames (relative effect TBC).
  - Match the track to the window frames; SKG frame colour TBC.
- **Living balcony (~560 wide):**
  - The drying rack is fixed to the concrete ceiling and must still lower. Keep the grille's top track at the outer edge, clear of the rack's plane.
  - The swing moves east–west, parallel to the façade. The seat and chains must not touch the cables at any point of the swing; cables flex inward under load, so measure the clearance on site (TBC).
- **Master balcony:** same spec, full height.
- **Cleaning:** soft cloth with water or mild detergent, then dry. Ask the MCST how outside glass cleaning is arranged.

## Condo rules & egress
- **MCST:**
  - BCA notes that works in strata developments may need MCST approval.
  - STB case law (Zou Xiong): child safety comes first and the MCST cannot refuse without good reason; it should publish design guidelines, and without them must assess each case on its merits.
- **'Condos allow only invisible grilles':** this is common practice, not law. Sengkang Grand's by-laws decide (TBC).
- **Fire:**
  - MHA says residential fire safety relies on fire compartments and staircases; balconies and windows are not statutory escape routes.
  - This research found no SCDF rule requiring residential grilles to be openable (TBC).
  - Firefighters can cut the cables with tools.
  - For balcony access, consider one openable section (costs more).

## To confirm
- Sengkang Grand by-laws: grille direction, colour, spacing, deposit, work hours
- Kid-room window type (top-hung or casement) and opening width
- Window frame colour
- Each installer's cable test report and quote

## Decision
- **Recommended: BLANCO PLEON 6 (white 521683)** (Singapore price TBC; Blanco dealer Hoe Kee) — inset SILGRANIT single bowl, bowl 54.5 × 40, 22 deep. The rim covers the stone cut-out, so no polished cut-out edge; the continuous tap ledge along the back has its own tap hole.
- **Colour**: white 521683 comes with a 3½" InFino waste set; soft white 527772 is the "for coloured components" version, sold without the waste set, so the colour-matched waste parts are bought separately.
- **Alternative (earlier suggestion): Franke Box BXX 210/110-54 (127.0677.190)** (S$650 at Econflo; web store shows it sold out) — choose it for stainless steel, undermount and no worry about heavy pots. Bowl 54 × 41, 20 deep, R12; the tap needs its own hole in the worktop.
- **Rejected: Franke Maris MRG 110-62** — undermount, and Franke specifies a worktop of at least 20 mm, so the 1.2 slab would need building up.
- **Rejected: Blanco Solis 500-U, Subline 500-U** — bowls only 50; the Subline 500-U starts at S$908.
- **Rejected: Franke Mythos MYX 110-55, Box 210-72, Felix FEX 110-70, Solis 700-U** — official minimum cabinet 80, so they don't fit the 71.9 cabinet.

## Criteria
- **Usable bowl size**: width ≥ 50, front-to-back ≥ 40, depth ≥ 18. A Ø28 stock pot is about 38 across its handles and must lie flat for rinsing.
- **Cabinet width**: official minimum cabinet ≤ 71.9 (scheme A sink cabinet 71.9, scheme B 76.9). The PLEON 6 needs 60, so both work.
- **Ease with a 1.2 sintered slab**: inset only needs a cut hole, hidden under the rim; undermount needs a polished cut-out edge and bonded fixings, and a non-through-body slab shows a different-colour edge.
- **Tap position**: the tap sits on the sink's ledge, so no extra hole in the stone.
- **Durability and noise**: granite composite is quiet and scratch-resistant but a dropped heavy pot can chip it; stainless shrugs off knocks but shows fine scratches.
- **Waste**: 3½" waste; the trap needs a dishwasher spigot.

## Do first
- **Quote and order**: WhatsApp Hoe Kee on +65 8779 5626 for the price and lead time of the BLANCO PLEON 6 white 521683 (its website lists only the PLEON 8 at S$642 and PLEON 9 at S$686, so the PLEON 6 must be asked for). See Blanco in person at Hoe Kee Superstore, 1 Jalan Berseh #01-09 to #01-13 New World Centre, daily 10:00–19:00.
- **For the stone fabricator**: cut the 59.5 × 49 hole from the template supplied with the sink; support the narrow strips of slab in front of and behind the cut-out on timber rails; seal under the rim with neutral-cure silicone.
- **For the carpenter**: add two rails across the top of the sink cabinet, front and back, to carry the slab and sink; drill the dishwasher hose hole at the lower back of the sink cabinet's side panel; keep the half-depth front shelf clear of the trap.
- **Tap**: choose a single-hole pull-out tap for the PLEON 6's tap hole; its height must clear the window sash's opening range.
- **Trap**: the waste set has no trap; buy one with a dishwasher spigot.

## Risks and open items
- PLEON 6 Singapore price, stock and warranty are **TBC**; European reference price €335 (Hornbach Austria).

- The PLEON 6 is 51 front-to-back; check the remaining front and back strips when the worktop depth is fixed.
- A dropped heavy pot can chip a granite-composite sink.
